virals.name: Joe Kent
virals.hook:
The illusion of choice and the inevitable return to war…

President Trump is being told that instead of choosing escalation or walking away, he has a sustainable third option in which he can maintain the blockade & threats of escalation without inviting blowback. 

It’s an illusion of choice that will inevitably force us back into war on Iran’s terms. 

It’s clear, and incredibly dangerous, that Trump’s decision making space and options are quietly being taken from him by his advisors who advocate for this blockade status quo. 

In reality, the President’s best & least destructive option is to deprive Iran of the leverage they currently have over us. He can do this by walking  away— first pull our troops & blockade from the region. Get them out of striking distance. Then, use the carrot & stick— impose sanctions, or lift them & un-freeze assets as leverage against the Iranians to get the SOH open. 

Keeping our troops in the region & maintaining the blockade only gives Iran targets to shoot at, and neither posture is worth that risk nor is sustainable long term. We’ve proven time and time over that we can project power from the U.S. when we need to. We can do it again if needed.

It’s highly unlikely that the blockade is going to result in the regime being overthrown or the Iranians capitulating—47 years of sanctions & an onslaught by Israel & the U.S. military have failed to achieve these results, and we’re naive to think that a blockade will accomplish anything but a military response from Iran. 

Iran is already messaging that they will not tolerate the current status quo of neither war nor peace. It’s only a matter of time until they retaliate by attempting to run the blockade and/or target our bases, or, if they feel threatened enough, target more gulf energy infrastructure, which will further harm the world’s economy & skyrocket prices at the pump for Americans. 

Pulling our blockade puts the ball back in Iran’s court—will they continue to shoot at ships once we’re out of the Gulf, or will Iran instead work with its neighbors to come up with a way to make the SOH work for the region? So far throughout this conflict, the Iranians have made it clear that public perception matters a great deal to them. It’s likely they’ll work peacefully with their Gulf neighbors to avoid being considered the chaos-agent. 

It’s clear that status quo is not a viable option. President Trump needs to accept that, ignore the advisors who’ve led him down this unwinnable path, and reset the playing field.

I discussed this & more with @MarioNawfal :

https://t.co/DCYv1ya4gC via @YouTube

A petition was recently registered in the UK Parliament that has structural flaws and false and misleading information, and will probably have harmful results.

6 UK citizens or legal residents can register a petition in Parliament; that is, one ordinary citizen as the registrant (in this case, a person named Saman Taherimood) plus 5 other ordinary citizens!

10 thousand signatures: the government is only obliged to respond.

100 thousand signatures: the petition is considered for a possible parliamentary debate, not that a debate is necessarily held!

5- The petition was written by an inexperienced person with no political track record.

Beware of currents that spend "the people of Iran" for their own interests! 🇮🇷

virals.name: OSINT Middle East Observer
virals.hook:
Evening update, Mon 23 Nov. Tehran picked a fight with its own mediator today. Iran reportedly summoned Qatar's envoy over a Qatar-Germany statement condemning Iranian attacks on the region, on the same day Qatar's prime minister was due to sit down with Rubio in Washington. I don't read it as Tehran dropping Doha. It's pressure on the go-between before he carries anything across.

Doha. The joint declaration came out of the Emir's state visit to Berlin on Saturday. It "strongly" condemns Iranian attacks on Qatar and its neighbours and rejects any move to close Hormuz. It also calls on Iran to stop arming the Houthis. Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei called it "surprising and regrettable". One MP went further and said Qatar can no longer mediate, but Baghaei's own line was the opposite: "Mediators, in any circumstances, continue their efforts". The ministry outranks a backbencher, so I'd take Baghaei's word for now.

Washington. The State Department said on Sunday that Rubio would host Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman today. There's no readout as I write. The backdrop isn't promising. Trump told Fox on Sunday that Iranian tankers trying the blockade would end up at the bottom of the sea, and that he's inclined to resume strikes after the new year if there's no deal. Israeli outlets disagree on timing: one reports Washington has pushed any strike back by at least a week, another says CENTCOM is at maximum readiness. Neither is confirmed.

Tehran. Baghaei said Iran "will use every means to counter US aggression" and called the blockade a breach of the UN Charter, while repeating that Hormuz could reopen quickly if sanctions and the blockade go. Speaker Ghalibaf said Iran can't stay in "neither war nor peace" indefinitely. To me that's the line of the day. He's telling his own side the stalemate has a cost.

Hormuz. I can't find a new UKMTO attack report for today as of early evening. Sunday's Gulf of Oman incident, a tanker and "military forces" near Chabahar, still has no ship, flag or navy named, and CENTCOM hasn't commented. Iran's navy claimed two tankers on fire near Hormuz on Sunday. No names, no confirmation.

Saudi Arabia. The Houthis claim they struck the Rabigh refinery on Sunday. Saudi authorities haven't confirmed any attack on a refinery. Houthi media also claim a Saudi-led strike in Hodeidah killed four people; Riyadh hasn't commented.

Markets. Brent was around $90.87, down 1.8%, at midday London time, with WTI near $82.02, down 1.6%. Oil falling after a weekend of claimed attacks on tankers and a refinery says the market isn't pricing a wider war yet.

Watch overnight: the State Department readout. If it mentions Hormuz or sequencing, Doha is still carrying a text. If it's just "regional developments", the mediation is stalling.

تاریخ به ما نشان می‌دهد که سازمان‌یافتگی اجتماعی و سیاسی جنبش می‌تواند به تثبیت جایگاه رهبری واحد ملی و سیاسی در عرصهٔ بین‌المللی و افزایش چشمگیر قدرت نفوذ و چانه‌زنی وی جهت جلب کمک خارجی برای آزادی میهن اشغالی یاری رساند.

بیش از سه سال پیش، جمعیت جمهوری‌خواهان حامی شاهزاده رضا پهلوی @prisp2023 بر پایهٔ چنین درک تاریخی از روند پیشبرد انقلاب ملی، بنیان نهاده شد؛ تا نشان دهد که برخلاف تبلیغات رژیم و پسمانده‌های انقلاب ارتجاعی فاجعه آمیز ۵۷، حداقل بخشی از جمهوری‌خواهان ایران‌گرای ترقی‌خواه و ضد رژیم، حامی رهبری واحد ملی و سیاسی شاهزاده رضا پهلوی هستند.

برای کسب پیروزی، گاه ناگزیریم از تجربه‌های موفق تاریخ درس بگیریم و آنها را تکرار کنیم.

outsiders.name: Joe Kent
outsiders.hook:
The illusion of choice and the inevitable return to war…

President Trump is being told that instead of choosing escalation or walking away, he has a sustainable third option in which he can maintain the blockade & threats of escalation without inviting blowback. 

It’s an illusion of choice that will inevitably force us back into war on Iran’s terms. 

It’s clear, and incredibly dangerous, that Trump’s decision making space and options are quietly being taken from him by his advisors who advocate for this blockade status quo. 

In reality, the President’s best & least destructive option is to deprive Iran of the leverage they currently have over us. He can do this by walking  away— first pull our troops & blockade from the region. Get them out of striking distance. Then, use the carrot & stick— impose sanctions, or lift them & un-freeze assets as leverage against the Iranians to get the SOH open. 

Keeping our troops in the region & maintaining the blockade only gives Iran targets to shoot at, and neither posture is worth that risk nor is sustainable long term. We’ve proven time and time over that we can project power from the U.S. when we need to. We can do it again if needed.

It’s highly unlikely that the blockade is going to result in the regime being overthrown or the Iranians capitulating—47 years of sanctions & an onslaught by Israel & the U.S. military have failed to achieve these results, and we’re naive to think that a blockade will accomplish anything but a military response from Iran. 

Iran is already messaging that they will not tolerate the current status quo of neither war nor peace. It’s only a matter of time until they retaliate by attempting to run the blockade and/or target our bases, or, if they feel threatened enough, target more gulf energy infrastructure, which will further harm the world’s economy & skyrocket prices at the pump for Americans. 

Pulling our blockade puts the ball back in Iran’s court—will they continue to shoot at ships once we’re out of the Gulf, or will Iran instead work with its neighbors to come up with a way to make the SOH work for the region? So far throughout this conflict, the Iranians have made it clear that public perception matters a great deal to them. It’s likely they’ll work peacefully with their Gulf neighbors to avoid being considered the chaos-agent. 

It’s clear that status quo is not a viable option. President Trump needs to accept that, ignore the advisors who’ve led him down this unwinnable path, and reset the playing field.

outsiders.original_en:
The illusion of choice and the inevitable return to war…

President Trump is being told that instead of choosing escalation or walking away, he has a sustainable third option in which he can maintain the blockade & threats of escalation without inviting blowback. 

It’s an illusion of choice that will inevitably force us back into war on Iran’s terms. 

It’s clear, and incredibly dangerous, that Trump’s decision making space and options are quietly being taken from him by his advisors who advocate for this blockade status quo. 

In reality, the President’s best & least destructive option is to deprive Iran of the leverage they currently have over us. He can do this by walking  away— first pull our troops & blockade from the region. Get them out of striking distance. Then, use the carrot & stick— impose sanctions, or lift them & un-freeze assets as leverage against the Iranians to get the SOH open. 

Keeping our troops in the region & maintaining the blockade only gives Iran targets to shoot at, and neither posture is worth that risk nor is sustainable long term. We’ve proven time and time over that we can project power from the U.S. when we need to. We can do it again if needed.

outsiders.original_en:
🚨 Warning

A petition was recently registered in the UK Parliament that has structural flaws and false and misleading information, and will probably have harmful results.

Before getting to the flaws, first an explanation of how petitions are registered in the UK Parliament:

6 UK citizens or legal residents can register a petition in Parliament; that is, one ordinary citizen as the registrant (in this case, a person named Saman Taherimood) plus 5 other ordinary citizens!

10 thousand signatures: the government is only obliged to respond.

100 thousand signatures: the petition is considered for a possible parliamentary debate, not that a debate is necessarily held!

❌ Flaws:

1- Citing polls by the disreputable GAMAAN institute and the Boroumand Foundation, the petition asks for the expulsion of diplomats and cutting cooperation with the Islamic Republic. (Lending credibility to fake statistics)

2- The petition claims 14 million people took part in the Dey protests and half of them called the name of Pahlavi; meaning only 7 million of Iran's 60 million population over 15 called the name "Pahlavi"!!!

Now suppose this petition succeeds. The first question for Parliament will be: why should we recognise Pahlavi as the opposition because of 11% of the population? This argument effectively discredits the Shah and the national opposition.

3- On the death toll, it cites the estimate of the left-wing British government, which puts the number killed at 12 to 20 thousand. Meanwhile the US president, Trump, announced a figure of 75 thousand killed and the petition could have cited that. (Downplaying the scale of the crime)

4- Britain has still not put the IRGC on its list of terrorist organisations and has only proscribed it. Under which law should Parliament cut ties with the regime?

This demand to cut cooperation with the regime without a clear legal explanation is more a political slogan than a reasoned parliamentary request.

5- The petition was written by an inexperienced person with no political track record.

6- The text of the petition is incomplete and amateurish, and has been promoted and endorsed by groups looking for funding and visibility.

Overall, this petition not only has serious flaws, but even if it reaches 100 thousand signatures, its results "could" end up harming Iran's national opposition led by Reza Shah II.

This petition is more about résumé-building and profile-building for the registrant than a calculated political demand; with whatever secondary aim (other than the people of Iran) may be behind it!

Beware of currents that spend "the people of Iran" for their own interests! 🇮🇷

outsiders.name: OSINT Middle East Observer
outsiders.hook:
Evening update, Mon 23 Nov. Tehran picked a fight with its own mediator today. Iran reportedly summoned Qatar's envoy over a Qatar-Germany statement condemning Iranian attacks on the region, on the same day Qatar's prime minister was due to sit down with Rubio in Washington. I don't read it as Tehran dropping Doha. It's pressure on the go-between before he carries anything across.

Doha. The joint declaration came out of the Emir's state visit to Berlin on Saturday. It "strongly" condemns Iranian attacks on Qatar and its neighbours and rejects any move to close Hormuz. It also calls on Iran to stop arming the Houthis. Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei called it "surprising and regrettable". One MP went further and said Qatar can no longer mediate, but Baghaei's own line was the opposite: "Mediators, in any circumstances, continue their efforts". The ministry outranks a backbencher, so I'd take Baghaei's word for now.

Washington. The State Department said on Sunday that Rubio would host Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman today. There's no readout as I write. The backdrop isn't promising. Trump told Fox on Sunday that Iranian tankers trying the blockade would end up at the bottom of the sea, and that he's inclined to resume strikes after the new year if there's no deal. Israeli outlets disagree on timing: one reports Washington has pushed any strike back by at least a week, another says CENTCOM is at maximum readiness. Neither is confirmed.

Tehran. Baghaei said Iran "will use every means to counter US aggression" and called the blockade a breach of the UN Charter, while repeating that Hormuz could reopen quickly if sanctions and the blockade go. Speaker Ghalibaf said Iran can't stay in "neither war nor peace" indefinitely. To me that's the line of the day. He's telling his own side the stalemate has a cost.

Hormuz. I can't find a new UKMTO attack report for today as of early evening. Sunday's Gulf of Oman incident, a tanker and "military forces" near Chabahar, still has no ship, flag or navy named, and CENTCOM hasn't commented. Iran's navy claimed two tankers on fire near Hormuz on Sunday. No names, no confirmation.

Saudi Arabia. The Houthis claim they struck the Rabigh refinery on Sunday. Saudi authorities haven't confirmed any attack on a refinery. Houthi media also claim a Saudi-led strike in Hodeidah killed four people; Riyadh hasn't commented.

Markets. Brent was around $90.87, down 1.8%, at midday London time, with WTI near $82.02, down 1.6%. Oil falling after a weekend of claimed attacks on tankers and a refinery says the market isn't pricing a wider war yet.

Watch overnight: the State Department readout. If it mentions Hormuz or sequencing, Doha is still carrying a text. If it's just "regional developments", the mediation is stalling.

هنگامیکه آمریکا و بریتانیا هنوز بر سر رهبری ژنرال دوگل بر نیروهای مبارز فرانسوی فعال علیه نازی‌ها طی جنگ جهانی دوم و نقش سیاسی شارل دوگل در آیندهٔ فرانسهٔ آزاد توافق نداشتند، ابتکار اتحاد جنبش‌های مبارز داخلی فرانسه در حمایت از رهبری ژنرال دوگل و تشکیل شورای ملی فرانسه، جایگاه وی را نزد متفقین به‌طور چشمگیری تقویت نمود و در روند پذیرش رهبری سیاسی ژنرال دوگل از سوی بریتانیای چرچیل و آمریکای روزولت نقش مهمی ایفا نمود.

تاریخ به ما نشان می‌دهد که سازمان‌یافتگی اجتماعی و سیاسی جنبش می‌تواند به تثبیت جایگاه رهبری واحد ملی و سیاسی در عرصهٔ بین‌المللی و افزایش چشمگیر قدرت نفوذ و چانه‌زنی وی جهت جلب کمک خارجی برای آزادی میهن اشغالی یاری رساند.

بیش از سه سال پیش، جمعیت جمهوری‌خواهان حامی شاهزاده رضا پهلوی @prisp2023 بر پایهٔ چنین درک تاریخی از روند پیشبرد انقلاب ملی، بنیان نهاده شد؛ تا نشان دهد که برخلاف تبلیغات رژیم و پسمانده‌های انقلاب ارتجاعی فاجعه آمیز ۵۷، حداقل بخشی از جمهوری‌خواهان ایران‌گرای ترقی‌خواه و ضد رژیم، حامی رهبری واحد ملی و سیاسی شاهزاده رضا پهلوی هستند.

برای کسب پیروزی، گاه ناگزیریم از تجربه‌های موفق تاریخ درس بگیریم و آنها را تکرار کنیم.

چنانچه جمهوری‌خواه و حامی انقلاب ملی شیروخورشید به رهبری شاهزاده رضا پهلوی هستید، به ما بپیوندید.

پاینده ایران

این است شعار ملی، رضا رضا پهلوی

History shows us that the social and political organisation of a movement can help consolidate the position of a single national and political leadership on the international stage and greatly increase its influence and bargaining power to win foreign help to free an occupied homeland.

More than three years ago, the Society of Republicans Supporting Prince Reza Pahlavi @prisp2023 was founded on this historical understanding of how a national revolution advances; to show that, contrary to the propaganda of the regime and the remnants of the catastrophic reactionary revolution of 1979, at least some of Iran's progressive, Iran-loving, anti-regime republicans support the single national and political leadership of Prince Reza Pahlavi.

To win, we sometimes have to learn from history's successful experiences and repeat them.

If you are a republican and a supporter of the Lion and Sun national revolution led by Prince Reza Pahlavi, join us.

Long live Iran

This is the national slogan: Reza, Reza Pahlavi
